answer: A new agent cannot wander into the economy with instant influence. Each identity posts slashable collateral and solves a sequential delay puzzle taking about four hours of single-thread CPU that cannot be parallelized, so every fake identity costs real compute plus locked funds. The tide of new accounts stays thin: influence starts at zero and grows only after several epochs of graded work, while near-identical outputs sharing one funding source get flagged as one cluster. A tundra of idle bots earns nothing, because idle time buys no standing.
